disclosure: Edited app capture sequence · synthetic test voice and readings

shots.caption: A low output does not explain itself.
shots.detail: Has the circuit changed, or is the measurement scaled? Choose a test that tells them apart.

shots.caption: “At ten kilohertz, output thirty-one millivolts.”
shots.detail: Synthetic input clip, transcribed by the real local Whisper model. Inference wait shortened.

shots.caption: Check the interpretation before it becomes evidence.
shots.detail: 10 kHz · 31 mVpp · fixed 2 Vpp input. The reading stays pending until confirmed.

shots.caption: “What would tell these apart?”
shots.detail: Both models fit the starting reading. Matching that one number does not choose a winner.

shots.caption: Different circuit response. Or a different amplitude scale.
shots.detail: One model changes R × C; the other preserves the nominal curve and scales its output.

shots.caption: At 80 Hz, their predictions separate.
shots.detail: Approximately 1.78 Vpp versus 0.197 Vpp. Chosen from a bounded frequency grid.

shots.caption: Benchlog saves the predictions before the next reading.
shots.detail: The receipt keeps the starting observation, setup and fitted models fixed.

shots.caption: “At eighty hertz, output one point seven eight volts.”
shots.detail: A second synthetic observation through real Whisper. Check it, then confirm.

shots.caption: Closer to the changed-time-constant example.
shots.detail: Compared with the saved prediction. Neither model is refitted to this answer.

scenes.title: Know what it cannot tell you

shots.caption: A model match is not proof of a faulty component.
shots.detail: The model sees R × C. It cannot tell which component changed.

shots.caption: Neither explanation is also a valid outcome.
shots.detail: Separate synthetic example: 0.8 Vpp at 80 Hz falls outside both comparison bands.

shots.caption: The original reading, prediction and result stay together.
shots.detail: Inspect the saved receipt. Speech uses AI; the comparisons are deterministic code.

shots.caption: A spoken observation. A reason for the next test.
